easy.statement_latex: Find the slant (oblique) asymptote of $f(x) = \dfrac{3x^2 - 2x - 3}{x - 2}$.
hints: Since the degree of the numerator is exactly one more than the degree of the denominator, there is a slant asymptote.
Use polynomial long division: divide the numerator by the denominator.
The quotient (ignoring the remainder) is the equation of the slant asymptote.
solution_steps_latex: Divide $3x^2 - 2x - 3$ by $x - 2$ using polynomial long division.
As $x \to \pm\infty$, the remainder term approaches $0$, so the slant asymptote is $y = 3x + 4$.
